speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. You mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and does it radiate to your jaw or teeth?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain you describe occurring while eating suggests possible irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve; is the discomfort also triggered by chewing or jaw movement? Additionally, do you notice any fluid draining from the ear or a sensation of fullness when wearing earrings?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain triggered by eating points toward auriculotemporal nerve irritation; is the shooting sensation also present when you tap on the tragus or the skin just in front of your ear canal? Do you notice any redness, swelling, or discharge from the ear canal or behind the ear?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (Tympanomandibular Syndrome)

Based on the normal otoscopy and negative tragus tap, the intact graft rules out infection or granulation tissue. The shooting pain triggered specifically by eating and chewing, in the absence of tragal tenderness, is classic for neuralgia involving the auriculotemporal nerve due to post-surgical irritation.
